prompt:

Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance. No flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face or plastic 3D-render finish. Keep this rendering exactly as in the attached image — the same finish, line, shading, skin and colour treatment.

Weather / season: a snowy night — snow drifting through warm lamplight outside.
Time of day: night — the scene lit by lamps, screens or windows, dark outside.

Outfit: a test pilot look fitted to her body — a silver heat-suit unzipped to the waist over a cropped sport top, slim gloves and a comm headset, showing her shoulders, collarbones and legs as far as the outfit allows, following her curvy figure — a slim waist and rounded hips; intimate areas covered.

Leave behind everything she wears in the attached image — no crown, tiara, helmet, feathers, headpiece, hairpins from it, armour or regalia; her hair is styled for the everyday outfit, with at most one small accessory.

Her element — tungsten: a dark steel-grey metal with the highest melting point of any metal, 3422 °C — it glows white-hot inside a light bulb as a filament and still does not melt; its old name wolfram means 'wolf's froth', because its ore devoured tin in the smelters' furnaces like a wolf, and tungsten is Swedish for 'heavy stone' — it is as heavy as gold; its carbide is nearly as hard as diamond; its ore scheelite glows bright blue-white under ultraviolet light; heavy, taciturn and unquenchable — may show in the outfit's details, motifs or small accessories.

Light: the place's own light, lit and coloured the way this style renders light and skin.

One figure in focus, natural hands with five fingers, no text, logo or watermark.
